sanskrit: sa karṇacāpaprabhavān iṣūn āśīviṣopamān bibhrad bhīmo mahārāja na jagāma vyathāṃ raṇe
english: Bearing the arrows loosed from Karṇa's bow, O great king—shafts like venomous serpents—Bhīma felt no flinch of distress in the battle.

sanskrit: tato dvātriṃśatā bhallair niśitais tigmatejanaiḥ vivyādha samare karṇaṃ bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān
english: Then with thirty-two whetted, keen-pointed broad-headed arrows the valorous Bhīmasena pierced Karṇa in the fight.

sanskrit: ayatnenaiva taṃ karṇaḥ śarair upa samākirat bhīmasenaṃ mahābāhuṃ saindhavasya vadhaiṣiṇam
english: With no effort at all Karṇa overwhelmed with his shafts the mighty-armed Bhīmasena, who sought the death of the Saindhava.

sanskrit: mṛdupūrvaṃ ca rādheyo bhīmam ājāv ayodhayat krodhapūrvaṃ tathā bhīmaḥ pūrvavairam anusmaran
english: Rādheya fought Bhīma in the battle gently at first, while Bhīma, recalling their old enmity, fought him in wrath.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmaseno nāmṛṣyad avamānam amarṣaṇaḥ sa tasmai vyasṛjat tūrṇaṃ śaravarṣam amitrajit
english: Bhīmasena, intolerant of insult, would not endure the slight; that conqueror of foes swiftly let loose a rain of arrows upon him.

sanskrit: te śarāḥ preṣitā rājan bhīmasenena saṃyuge nipetuḥ sarvato bhīmāḥ kūjanta iva pakṣiṇaḥ
english: Those arrows sped by Bhīmasena in the fray, O king, fearsome and falling on every side, screamed like birds in flight.

sanskrit: hemapuṅkhā mahārāja bhīmasenadhanuścyutāḥ abhyadravaṃs te rādheyaṃ vṛkāḥ kṣudramṛgaṃ yathā
english: Gold-feathered, O great king, sped from Bhīmasena's bow, they rushed upon Rādheya as wolves upon a lesser beast.

sanskrit: karṇas tu rathināṃ śreṣṭhaś chādyamānaḥ samantataḥ rājan vyasṛjad ugrāṇi śaravarṣāṇi saṃyuge
english: But Karṇa, foremost of chariot-warriors, covered on every side, O king, loosed in turn his own fierce showers of arrows in the fight.

sanskrit: tasya tān aśaniprakhyān iṣūn samaraśobhinaḥ ciccheda bahubhir bhallair asaṃprāptān vṛkodaraḥ
english: Those shafts of his, like thunderbolts, splendid in battle, Vṛkodara cut down with many broad-headed arrows before they reached him.

sanskrit: punaś ca śaravarṣeṇa chādayām āsa bhārata karṇo vaikartano yuddhe bhīmasenaṃ mahāratham
english: And again, O Bhārata, Karṇa Vaikartana covered the great chariot-warrior Bhīmasena with a rain of arrows in the fight.

sanskrit: tatra bhārata bhīmaṃ tu dṛṣṭavantaḥ sma sāyakaiḥ samācitatanuṃ saṃkhye śvāvidhaṃ śalalair iva
english: There, O Bhārata, we beheld Bhīma in the battle, his body bristling with arrows like a porcupine with its quills.

sanskrit: hemapuṅkhāñ śilādhautān karṇacāpacyutāñ śarān dadhāra samare vīraḥ svaraśmīn iva bhāskaraḥ
english: Gold-feathered, stone-whetted shafts sped from Karṇa's bow the hero bore in battle, as the sun bears its own rays.

sanskrit: rudhirokṣitasarvāṅgo bhīmaseno vyarocata tapanīyanibhaiḥ puṣpaiḥ palāśa iva kānane
english: His every limb drenched with blood, Bhīmasena shone like a palāśa tree in the forest with its blossoms bright as gold.

sanskrit: tat tu bhīmo mahārāja karṇasya caritaṃ raṇe nāmṛṣyata maheṣvāsaḥ krodhād udvṛtya cakṣuṣī
english: But Bhīma, O great king, that mighty archer, did not endure this deed of Karṇa's in the battle, and in his wrath he rolled his eyes.

sanskrit: sa karṇaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā nārācānāṃ samārpayat mahīdharam iva śvetaṃ gūḍhapādair viṣolbaṇaiḥ
english: He struck Karṇa with twenty-five iron shafts—as one strikes a white mountain—shafts whose barbs lay hidden and whose touch was venomous.

sanskrit: taṃ vivyādha punar bhīmaḥ ṣaḍbhir aṣṭābhir eva ca marmasv amaravikrāntaḥ sūtaputraṃ mahāraṇe
english: Then Bhīma, valiant as a god, pierced the son of the charioteer once more, with six and then with eight shafts in his vital points in that great battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇasya saṃkruddho bhīmasenaḥ pratāpavān ciccheda kārmukaṃ tūrṇaṃ sarvopakaraṇāni ca
english: Then the valorous Bhīmasena, full of fury, swiftly cut to pieces Karṇa's bow and all its fittings.

sanskrit: jaghāna caturaś cāśvān sūtaṃ ca tvaritaḥ śaraiḥ nārācair arkaraśmyābhaiḥ karṇaṃ vivyādha corasi
english: In haste he slew his four horses and his charioteer with arrows, and with iron shafts bright as the sun's rays he pierced Karṇa in the breast.

sanskrit: te jagmur dharaṇīṃ sarve karṇaṃ nirbhidya māriṣa yathā hi jaladaṃ bhittvā rājan sūryasya raśmayaḥ
english: All those shafts, having pierced Karṇa through, sank into the earth, O sir, as the rays of the sun pass through and beyond a cloud, O king.

sanskrit: sa vaikalyaṃ mahat prāpya chinnadhanvā śarārditaḥ tathā puruṣamānī sa pratyapāyād rathāntaram
english: Reduced to great helplessness, his bow severed and tormented by arrows, that proud man, full of manhood as he was, withdrew to another chariot.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca yasmiñ jayāśā satataṃ putrāṇāṃ mama saṃjaya taṃ dṛṣṭvā vimukhaṃ saṃkhye kiṃ nu duryodhano 'bravīt karṇo vā samare tāta kim akārṣīd ataḥ param
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: He in whom my sons forever placed their hope of victory, Saṃjaya—seeing him turned away from the battle, what then did Duryodhana say, and what, my son, did Karṇa do next in the fight?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīmasenaṃ raṇe dṛṣṭvā jvalantam iva pāvakam ratham anyaṃ samāsthāya vidhivat kalpitaṃ punaḥ abhyayāt pāṇḍavaṃ karṇo vātoddhūta ivārṇavaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding Bhīmasena in the battle blazing like fire, Karṇa mounted another chariot duly equipped and rushed again upon the Pāṇḍava, like the ocean lashed by the wind.

sanskrit: kruddham ādhirathiṃ dṛṣṭvā putrās tava viśāṃ pate bhīmasenam amanyanta vaivasvatamukhe hutam
english: Seeing the son of Adhiratha enraged, O lord of peoples, your sons reckoned Bhīmasena as already offered into the mouth of the son of Vivasvat.

sanskrit: cāpaśabdaṃ mahat kṛtvā talaśabdaṃ ca bhairavam abhyavartata rādheyo bhīmasenarathaṃ prati
english: Making a great twang of his bow and a terrible slap of his palm, Rādheya bore down upon Bhīmasena's chariot.

sanskrit: punar eva tato rājan mahān āsīt sudāruṇaḥ vimardaḥ sūtaputrasya bhīmasya ca viśāṃ pate
english: Then once more, O king, there arose a great and most dreadful clash between the son of the charioteer and Bhīma, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: saṃrabdhau hi mahābāhū parasparavadhaiṣiṇau anyonyam īkṣāṃ cakrāte dahantāv iva locanaiḥ
english: For those two mighty-armed warriors, enraged and each seeking the other's death, gazed upon one another as though they would burn each other with their eyes.

sanskrit: krodharaktekṣaṇau kruddhau niḥśvasantau mahārathau yuddhe 'nyonyaṃ samāsādya tatakṣatur ariṃdamau
english: Their eyes red with wrath, both enraged and breathing hard, those great chariot-warriors, those tamers of foes, closing on each other in the fight, hewed at one another.

sanskrit: vyāghrāv iva susaṃrabdhau śyenāv iva ca śīghragau śarabhāv iva saṃkruddhau yuyudhāte parasparam
english: Furious as two tigers, swift as two hawks, raging as two śarabhas, they fought with one another.

sanskrit: tato bhīmaḥ smaran kleśān akṣadyūte vane 'pi ca virāṭanagare caiva prāptaṃ duḥkham ariṃdamaḥ
english: Then Bhīma, that tamer of foes, recalled the torments suffered at the dice-game and in the forest too, and the misery endured in the city of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: rāṣṭrāṇāṃ sphītaratnānāṃ haraṇaṃ ca tavātmajaiḥ satataṃ ca parikleśān saputreṇa tvayā kṛtān
english: And the seizing of their kingdoms, rich in jewels, by your sons, and the unending torments inflicted by you together with your son—

sanskrit: dagdhum aicchaś ca yat kuntīṃ saputrāṃ tvam anāgasam kṛṣṇāyāś ca parikleśaṃ sabhāmadhye durātmabhiḥ
english: How you sought to burn Kuntī, guiltless, together with her sons, and the abuse of Kṛṣṇā in the midst of the assembly by those wicked men—

sanskrit: patim anyaṃ parīpsasva na santi patayas tava narakaṃ patitāḥ pārthāḥ sarve ṣaṇḍhatilopamāḥ
english: "Seek another husband; your husbands are no more; the Pārthas are all fallen into hell, like seeds of sesame without kernel."

sanskrit: samakṣaṃ tava kauravya yad ūcuḥ kuravas tadā dāsībhogena kṛṣṇāṃ ca bhoktukāmāḥ sutās tava
english: What the Kurus said then before your eyes, O Kaurava, when your sons desired to use Kṛṣṇā as a bondwoman to be enjoyed—

sanskrit: yac cāpi tān pravrajataḥ kṛṣṇājinanivāsinaḥ paruṣāṇy uktavān karṇaḥ sabhāyāṃ saṃnidhau tava
english: And the harsh words Karṇa spoke against them as they set forth into exile, clothed in black antelope-skins, there in the assembly, in your presence—

sanskrit: tṛṇīkṛtya ca yat pārthāṃs tava putro vavalga ha viṣamasthān samastho hi saṃrambhād gatacetasaḥ
english: And how, counting the Pārthas as so much straw, your son had exulted—he, secure himself, over them in their distress, his wits gone in his fury—

sanskrit: bālyāt prabhṛti cārighnas tāni duḥkhāni cintayan niravidyata dharmātmā jīvitena vṛkodaraḥ
english: Brooding on these sorrows from his childhood on, that slayer of foes, the righteous Vṛkodara, grew weary of his very life.

sanskrit: tato visphārya sumahad dhemapṛṣṭhaṃ durāsadam cāpaṃ bharataśārdūlas tyaktātmā karṇam abhyayāt
english: Then, drawing his great gold-backed and unassailable bow, that tiger of the Bhāratas, careless of his own life, rushed upon Karṇa.

sanskrit: sa sāyakamayair jālair bhīmaḥ karṇarathaṃ prati bhānumadbhiḥ śilādhautair bhānoḥ pracchādayat prabhām
english: With nets of arrows, gleaming and stone-whetted, Bhīma cloaked Karṇa's chariot and veiled the very radiance of the sun.

sanskrit: tataḥ prahasyādhirathis tūrṇam asyañ śitāñ śarān vyadhamad bhīmasenasya śarajālāni patribhiḥ
english: Then the son of Adhiratha, laughing, swiftly hurling his keen shafts, scattered Bhīmasena's nets of arrows with his own feathered ones.

sanskrit: mahāratho mahābāhur mahāvegair mahābalaḥ vivyādhādhirathir bhīmaṃ navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: The great chariot-warrior, mighty-armed and mighty in strength, the son of Adhiratha, pierced Bhīma with nine swift and whetted arrows.

sanskrit: sa tottrair iva mātaṅgo vāryamāṇaḥ patatribhiḥ abhyadhāvad asaṃbhrāntaḥ sūtaputraṃ vṛkodaraḥ
english: Like an elephant goaded with hooks, held back by those winged shafts, Vṛkodara, undismayed, charged at the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena rabhasaṃ pāṇḍavarṣabham karṇaḥ pratyudyayau yoddhuṃ matto mattam iva dvipam
english: As that bull of the Pāṇḍavas rushed on swift and impetuous, Karṇa advanced to meet him in combat, as one rutting elephant meets another.

sanskrit: tataḥ pradhmāpya jalajaṃ bherīśatanināditam akṣubhyata balaṃ harṣād uddhūta iva sāgaraḥ
english: Then, his conch blown and a hundred kettledrums resounding, the host was stirred with joy, like the ocean upheaved.

sanskrit: tad uddhūtaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭva rathanāgāśvapattimat bhīmaḥ karṇaṃ samāsādya chādayām āsa sāyakaiḥ
english: Seeing that host upheaved, with its chariots, elephants, horses, and foot, Bhīma closed with Karṇa and covered him with arrows.

sanskrit: aśvān ṛśyasavarṇāṃs tu haṃsavarṇair hayottamaiḥ vyāmiśrayad raṇe karṇaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ chādayañ śaraiḥ
english: Karṇa, his horses the color of the antelope, mingled them in battle with the swan-white steeds of the Pāṇḍava as he covered him with shafts.

sanskrit: ṛśyavarṇān hayān karkair miśrān mārutaraṃhasaḥ nirīkṣya tava putrāṇāṃ hāhākṛtam abhūd balam
english: Seeing the antelope-hued horses mingled with the white ones, swift as the wind, the host of your sons broke into cries of dismay.

sanskrit: te hayā bahv aśobhanta miśritā vātaraṃhasaḥ sitāsitā mahārāja yathā vyomni balāhakāḥ
english: Those horses, swift as the wind, mingled together, shone in their multitude, white and dark, O great king, like clouds in the sky.

sanskrit: saṃrabdhau krodhatāmrākṣau prekṣya karṇavṛkodarau saṃtrastāḥ samakampanta tvadīyānāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Beholding Karṇa and Vṛkodara enraged, their eyes copper-red with wrath, the great chariot-warriors of your side trembled in terror.

sanskrit: yamarāṣṭropamaṃ ghoram āsīd āyodhanaṃ tayoḥ durdarśaṃ bharataśreṣṭha pretarājapuraṃ yathā
english: The battlefield of those two was terrible as the realm of Yama, hard to look upon, O best of the Bhāratas, like the city of the king of the dead.

sanskrit: samājam iva tac citraṃ prekṣamāṇā mahārathāḥ nālakṣayañ jayaṃ vyaktam ekaikasya nivāraṇe
english: Watching that wondrous spectacle as if it were a festival, the great chariot-warriors could not clearly discern victory for either in the warding off of the other.

sanskrit: tayoḥ praikṣanta saṃmardaṃ saṃnikṛṣṭamahāstrayoḥ tava durmantrite rājan saputrasya viśāṃ pate
english: They watched the clash of those two, their great weapons drawn close, a clash born of your ill counsel, O king, yours and your son's, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: chādayantau hi śatrughnāv anyonyaṃ sāyakaiḥ śitaiḥ śarajālāvṛtaṃ vyoma cakrāte śaravṛṣṭibhiḥ
english: Those two slayers of foes, covering one another with keen arrows, made the sky veiled with nets of shafts by their showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tāv anyonyaṃ jighāṃsantau śarais tīkṣṇair mahārathau prekṣaṇīyatarāv āstāṃ vṛṣṭimantāv ivāmbudau
english: Those two great chariot-warriors, each striving to slay the other with sharp arrows, were a most beautiful sight, like two rain-laden clouds pouring down.

sanskrit: suvarṇavikṛtān bāṇān pramuñcantāv ariṃdamau bhāsvaraṃ vyoma cakrāte vahnyulkābhir iva prabho
english: Loosing arrows wrought with gold, those two tamers of foes made the sky blaze as if with falling meteors of fire, O lord.

sanskrit: tābhyāṃ muktā vyakāśanta kaṅkabarhiṇavāsasaḥ paṅktyaḥ śaradi mattānāṃ sārasānām ivāmbare
english: Loosed by the two, the shafts fledged with heron and peacock feathers shone in their rows, like flights of exultant cranes in the autumn sky.

sanskrit: saṃsaktaṃ sūtaputreṇa dṛṣṭvā bhīmam ariṃdamam atibhāram amanyetāṃ bhīme kṛṣṇadhanaṃjayau
english: Seeing Bhīma, that tamer of foes, locked in combat with the son of the charioteer, Kṛṣṇa and Dhanaṃjaya thought the burden upon Bhīma too great.

sanskrit: tatrādhirathibhīmābhyāṃ śarair muktair dṛḍhāhatāḥ iṣupātam atikramya petur aśvanaradvipāḥ
english: There, struck hard by the arrows loosed by the son of Adhiratha and by Bhīma, horses, men, and elephants fell beyond even the range of the shafts.

sanskrit: patadbhiḥ patitaiś cānyair gatāsubhir anekaśaḥ kṛto mahān mahārāja putrāṇāṃ te janakṣayaḥ
english: By the many falling and fallen, lifeless beyond number, a great slaughter was wrought, O great king, among the people of your sons.

sanskrit: manuṣyāśvagajānāṃ ca śarīrair gatajīvitaiḥ kṣaṇena bhūmiḥ saṃjajñe saṃvṛtā bharatarṣabha
english: In an instant the earth was covered over with the lifeless bodies of men, horses, and elephants, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca atyadbhutam ahaṃ manye bhīmasenasya vikramam yat karṇaṃ yodhayām āsa samare laghuvikramam
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Most wondrous I deem the prowess of Bhīmasena, in that he made Karṇa, deft and swift in battle, give fight to him.

sanskrit: tridaśān api codyuktān sarvaśastradharān yudhi vārayed yo raṇe karṇaḥ sayakṣāsuramānavān
english: That Karṇa, who in battle could hold off even the thirty gods arrayed for war and bearing every weapon, together with yakṣas, asuras, and men—

sanskrit: sa kathaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ yuddhe bhrājamānam iva śriyā nātarat saṃyuge tāta tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: How could he not overcome the Pāṇḍava in the fight, who shone as if with glory in the battle? Tell me that, my son Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: kathaṃ ca yuddhaṃ bhūyo 'bhūt tayoḥ prāṇadurodare atra manye samāyatto jayo vājaya eva vā
english: And how did the battle between those two unfold once more, that desperate gamble for life? On this, I think, hangs victory or defeat.

sanskrit: karṇaṃ prāpya raṇe sūta mama putraḥ suyodhanaḥ jetum utsahate pārthān sagovindān sasātvatān
english: Having Karṇa in the battle, O charioteer, my son Suyodhana dares to hope he can conquer the Pārthas, together with Govinda and the Sātvatas.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu nirjitaṃ karṇam asakṛd bhīmakarmaṇā bhīmasenena samare moha āviśatīva mām
english: But hearing that Karṇa was vanquished, and not once only, by Bhīmasena of dreadful deeds in the battle, a daze well-nigh overcomes me.

sanskrit: vinaṣṭān kauravān manye mama putrasya durnayaiḥ na hi karṇo maheṣvāsān pārthāñ jyeṣyati saṃjaya
english: Undone I deem the Kauravas through the misrule of my son; for Karṇa will not vanquish the Pārthas, those mighty archers, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: kṛtavān yāni yuddhāni karṇaḥ pāṇḍusutaiḥ saha sarvatra pāṇḍavāḥ karṇam ajayanta raṇājire
english: In all the battles Karṇa has waged with the sons of Pāṇḍu, everywhere the Pāṇḍavas have defeated Karṇa on the field of war.

sanskrit: ajayyāḥ pāṇḍavās tāta devair api savāsavaiḥ na ca tad budhyate mandaḥ putro duryodhano mama
english: Unconquerable are the Pāṇḍavas, my son, even by the gods with Vāsava among them; yet my dull-witted son Duryodhana does not perceive it.

sanskrit: dhanaṃ dhaneśvarasyeva hṛtvā pārthasya me sutaḥ madhuprepsur ivābuddhiḥ prapātaṃ nāvabudhyate
english: Having seized the wealth of Pārtha as one might seize the wealth of the lord of riches, my foolish son, like a man greedy for honey, does not see the fall before him.

sanskrit: nikṛtyā nikṛtiprajño rājyaṃ hṛtvā mahātmanām jitān ity eva manvānaḥ pāṇḍavān avamanyate
english: Skilled in fraud, having stolen by fraud the kingdom of those great-souled ones, and reckoning them already conquered, he holds the Pāṇḍavas in contempt.

sanskrit: putrasnehābhibhūtena mayā cāpy akṛtātmanā dharme sthitā mahātmāno nikṛtāḥ pāṇḍunandanāḥ
english: And by me too, overborne by love for my son and undisciplined in soul, were the great-souled sons of Pāṇḍu, steadfast in dharma, wronged.

sanskrit: śamakāmaḥ sadā pārtho dīrghaprekṣī yudhiṣṭhiraḥ aśakta iti manvānaiḥ putrair mama nirākṛtaḥ
english: Pārtha Yudhiṣṭhira, ever desiring peace and far-sighted, was spurned by my sons, who reckoned him powerless.

sanskrit: tāni duḥkhāny anekāni viprakārāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ hṛdi kṛtvā mahābāhur bhīmo 'yudhyata sūtajam
english: Taking all those manifold sorrows and outrages to heart, the mighty-armed Bhīma fought the son of the charioteer.

sanskrit: tasmān me saṃjaya brūhi karṇabhīmau yathā raṇe ayudhyetāṃ yudhi śreṣṭhau parasparavadhaiṣiṇau
english: Therefore tell me, Saṃjaya, how Karṇa and Bhīma, those two foremost in war, fought in the battle, each seeking the other's death.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan yathā vṛttaḥ saṃgrāmaḥ karṇabhīmayoḥ parasparavadhaprepsvor vane kuñjarayor iva
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king, how the combat unfolded between Karṇa and Bhīma, each seeking the other's death, like two elephants in the forest.

sanskrit: rājan vaikartano bhīmaṃ kruddhaḥ kruddham ariṃdamam parākrāntaṃ parākramya vivyādha triṃśatā śaraiḥ
english: O king, Vaikartana, enraged, advancing in valor upon Bhīma the tamer of foes—enraged and valiant in turn—pierced him with thirty arrows.

sanskrit: mahāvegaiḥ prasannāgraiḥ śātakumbhapariṣkṛtaiḥ āhanad bharataśreṣṭha bhīmaṃ vaikartanaḥ śaraiḥ
english: With swift, bright-pointed arrows adorned with gold, Vaikartana struck Bhīma, O best of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tasyāsyato dhanur bhīmaś cakarta niśitais tribhiḥ rathanīḍāc ca yantāraṃ bhallenāpātayat kṣitau
english: As he loosed his shafts, Bhīma cut his bow with three whetted arrows, and with a broad-headed shaft struck his driver down from the chariot-seat to the ground.

sanskrit: sa kāṅkṣan bhīmasenasya vadhaṃ vaikartano vṛṣaḥ śaktiṃ kanakavaiḍūryacitradaṇḍāṃ parāmṛśat
english: Then Vaikartana, that bull among men, longing for Bhīmasena's death, laid hold of a spear with a shaft bright with gold and lapis.

sanskrit: pragṛhya ca mahāśaktiṃ kālaśaktim ivāparām samutkṣipya ca rādheyaḥ saṃdhāya ca mahābalaḥ cikṣepa bhīmasenāya jīvitāntakarīm iva
english: Grasping that great spear, like a second spear of Death, the mighty Rādheya raised it, took his aim, and hurled it at Bhīmasena, as though to make an end of his life.
